prospects.name: JFrog

score_rationale.timing: CMO Genefa Murphy appointed Jan 5 2026 for a declared 'next growth phase'; FY2027 brand-budget planning is forming now.
score_rationale.capacity: FY2025 revenue $531.8M (+24%), $704.4M cash, $142.3M free cash flow, NDR 118%. A $3-5M/yr deal is immaterial to the balance sheet.
score_rationale.brand_fit: No software-supply-chain-security brand is on the F1 grid (Confluent = data streaming). JFrog can OWN the category. Murphy's own thesis - 'trust, control, discipline at velocity' - is a literal motorsport metaphor, and she personally built the Udemy x McLaren deal.
score_rationale.urgency: Rivals Sonatype/Snyk are circling the same whitespace; first-mover locks the category for 3 years.

prospects.headline: The CMO who built the Udemy-McLaren deal now runs marketing at JFrog - and the software-supply-chain-security grid slot is empty.
prospects.the_case: On 5 January 2026 JFrog appointed Genefa Murphy as Chief Marketing Officer for what the company explicitly called its 'next growth phase' in AI-driven software supply chain management. Murphy is the single most important signal in this brief: at Udemy she personally architected the multi-series McLaren Racing partnership (F1, IndyCar, NEOM McLaren Formula E and Extreme E). She is a proven, repeat motorsport-sponsorship believer who now controls the brand budget of a company with $531.8M revenue (+24% YoY), $704.4M of cash, and $142.3M of free cash flow. Crucially, her public thesis for JFrog - that 'as velocity increases there is an increasing need for trust, control and discipline across the software supply chain' - is a ready-made Formula 1 narrative. And the category is wide open: Confluent (data streaming) sits on Williams, but no software-supply-chain-security brand is anywhere on the grid. JFrog can be first and own it.
prospects.why_now: Murphy is ~5 months into a mandate defined as a growth-phase reset, the exact moment a CMO sets the multi-year brand-investment agenda and shapes the next fiscal year's budget. She has done an F1/FE deal before, so there is no education curve - the internal objection ('does motorsport work for B2B?') is already answered by her own track record. Move while the category whitespace is still empty and before a DevSecOps rival (Sonatype, Snyk, GitLab) plants a flag first.
prospects.why_team: McLaren is the warm path: Murphy already knows the McLaren commercial organisation intimately from the Udemy partnership, and McLaren's technology-forward, precision-engineering identity mirrors JFrog's 'secure software, shipped fast' promise. If McLaren's category is constrained, Aston Martin offers premium enterprise gravitas (its buyer is the CISO/CTO JFrog sells to) and an open DevSecOps slot. Either team places JFrog's 'from code to chequered flag' supply-chain-integrity story in front of exactly the enterprise IT decision-makers it needs.
prospects.deal_architecture: Recommended entry: associate / official partner tier on McLaren (relationship-led) or Aston Martin, securing car and suit branding rights in the software-supply-chain-security category, garage access, B2B hospitality and digital inventory. Structure across a MINIMUM OF THREE YEARS at an estimated $3-5M/yr, calibrated to JFrog's confirmed $531.8M revenue base and $704M cash position, with a category-exclusivity clause so no DevSecOps rival can follow.

decision_maker.name: Genefa Murphy, PhD
decision_maker.title: Chief Marketing Officer, JFrog (appointed Jan 5 2026)
decision_maker.bio: Former Chief Marketing & Content Officer at Udemy, where she built the multi-series McLaren Racing partnership. Previously CMO of Five9, SVP & CMO of Micro Focus, and Global VP Corporate Marketing & Communications at Hewlett Packard Enterprise. A repeat motorsport-sponsorship dealmaker who now owns JFrog's brand budget.

prospects.opening_angle: Open on what she already knows: "You proved at Udemy that an F1 grid is a B2B channel, not a billboard. The software-supply-chain-security slot is still empty - JFrog can own the category McLaren's tech partners can't. Which 25-minute window do you want to take?"

risks.title: BUDGET CYCLE LAG
risks.detail: Murphy may not have a discretionary brand-sponsorship line approved until the FY2027 cycle.
risks.counter: Frame as a strategic, founder-level category play and offer a short-form LOI to hold category exclusivity now while the budget formalises.

risks.title: MARKETING vs FOUNDER ALIGNMENT
risks.detail: JFrog's founder-CEO Shlomi Ben Haim is hands-on; a marquee spend needs his buy-in.
risks.counter: Position it as a category-ownership land-grab (trust/security is JFrog's core message) - a CEO narrative, not just a marketing line item.

risks.title: B2B SKEPTICISM
risks.detail: Investors may question motorsport spend at a profit-inflecting software company.
risks.counter: Murphy's Udemy-McLaren results are the proof case; lead with measured B2B pipeline outcomes, not impressions.

prospects.name: SnapLogic
prospects.ticker: Private (a16z, Microsoft, Silver Lake Waterman, Sixth Street, Capital One Ventures)

score_rationale.timing: President Molly Matthews appointed May 12 2026; honeymoon window now narrowing (brief originally issued May 12).
score_rationale.capacity: $100M+ ARR confirmed Aug 2025, a16z-backed balance sheet.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Agentic integration maps to F1 precision; direct counter-narrative to Confluent.
score_rationale.urgency: Confluent (direct iPaaS rival) is on the Williams 2026 livery; association hardens every race weekend.

prospects.headline: SnapLogic appointed a President and expanded its C-suite the same day; rival Confluent is already on the Williams livery.
prospects.the_case: On 12 May 2026 SnapLogic appointed Molly Matthews (ex-Microsoft enterprise GTM) as President while simultaneously promoting its Chief Customer Officer and Chief People Officer - a deliberate scale-up posture with new budget authority and appetite for brand investment. Backed by a16z, Microsoft, Silver Lake Waterman, Sixth Street and Capital One Ventures, with $100M+ ARR confirmed Aug 2025 and customers including AstraZeneca, Adobe, Verizon and Sony. The decisive signal: Confluent, a direct iPaaS rival, is an active partner on the Williams 2026 livery - SnapLogic cannot cede motorsport's enterprise-credibility stage to a competitor.
prospects.why_now: Matthews's appointment created a leadership window in which new Presidents approve first-mover brand investments to set GTM identity; meanwhile Confluent's Williams presence hardens with every race. A rival-team announcement reframes the narrative before Confluent's association solidifies.
prospects.why_team: Pitch McLaren or Aston Martin to place SnapLogic directly opposite Confluent's Williams partnership - turning a competitor's sponsorship into SnapLogic's urgency argument, in front of the same CTO/CDO audience.
prospects.deal_architecture: Associate partner tier on McLaren or Aston Martin: garage access, digital inventory and B2B hospitality across the calendar. NOTE: re-architect to a MINIMUM THREE-YEAR commitment (the original May 12 brief proposed two years) at an estimated $3-5M/yr, calibrated to $100M+ ARR and an a16z-backed balance sheet.

decision_maker.name: Molly Matthews
decision_maker.title: President, SnapLogic (appointed May 12 2026)
decision_maker.bio: Former Microsoft enterprise GTM leader with deep experience scaling commercial organisations globally. First major brand-investment decisions fall within her new mandate and budget authority.

prospects.opening_angle: Open on the Confluent-Williams livery, then ask: "Your closest competitor just bought a car. Which grid slot is SnapLogic taking in the next 25 minutes - for the next three years?"

risks.title: BUDGET NOT YET UNLOCKED
risks.detail: Matthews is weeks into the role; formal budget cycles may lag.
risks.counter: Frame as a founder-level decision needing only CEO + President alignment; offer a short-form LOI to hold inventory.

risks.title: CONFLUENT EXCLUSIVITY CLAUSE
risks.detail: Williams may hold category exclusivity for data-integration vendors.
risks.counter: That is the argument for McLaren or Aston Martin - exclusivity at a rival team is a feature, not a barrier.

risks.title: ENTERPRISE BRAND CONSERVATISM
risks.detail: A CTO/CDO buyer may view motorsport as frivolous.
risks.counter: Confluent's Williams presence proves the category has already validated F1 as a B2B channel.

prospects.name: Quantinuum

score_rationale.timing: IPO roadshow is a once-only brand-elevation moment - the company is buying public-market visibility right now.
score_rationale.capacity: Honeywell spin-off targeting a ~$12.7B IPO valuation (27% premium over its $10B Sept 2025 round). Capacity is not a constraint.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Quantum = ultimate precision/compute narrative; not literally in the car, but a championship-compute / R&D halo play. Anglo-American footprint suits a British team.
score_rationale.urgency: No direct quantum rival on the grid; the forcing function is the IPO window itself.

prospects.headline: Honeywell spin-off Quantinuum is heading for a ~$12.7B IPO - a textbook overnight unicorn with a brand-elevation budget and no motorsport history.
prospects.the_case: Quantinuum is the highest-priority class of target in our mandate: a born-big spin-off (from Honeywell) heading into a ~$12.7B IPO, up 27% on its $10B September 2025 valuation. An IPO is a one-time brand-elevation moment, and an F1 association is among the fastest ways for a deep-tech company to acquire global enterprise visibility. It has never entered motorsport, so it would not be the 100th brand in the inbox.
prospects.why_now: The IPO roadshow is the window: leadership is actively investing in public-market visibility and enterprise credibility. A multi-year F1 engineering-partner deal signed around the listing compounds the narrative.
prospects.why_team: Aston Martin (premium, engineering gravitas) or a British engineering-led team aligns Quantinuum's Anglo-American identity with a precision/compute halo - 'the quantum edge in performance R&D.'
prospects.deal_architecture: Engineering / official technology partner tier, minimum three years, estimated $3-6M/yr, positioned as an R&D-and-brand halo around the listing, with category exclusivity for quantum computing.

decision_maker.name: Quantinuum CMO / Head of Brand (verify current holder)
decision_maker.title: Marketing / Brand leadership
decision_maker.bio: Confirm the current CMO/brand lead and IPO communications owner before outreach; the CFO and IR team are co-decision-makers during the listing window.

prospects.opening_angle: "You get one IPO. An F1 engineering partnership turns your listing from a finance event into a global brand moment - and quantum is the one category no rival on the grid can claim."

risks.title: IPO QUIET PERIOD
risks.detail: Securities rules may restrict marketing spend/announcements around the listing.
risks.counter: Structure the agreement to sign quietly and activate post-listing; use the roadshow to build internal consensus.

risks.title: DEEP-TECH BRAND CAUTION
risks.detail: A quantum firm may see F1 as off-strategy.
risks.counter: Position as enterprise-credibility and talent-attraction, not consumer marketing.

prospects.name: Schneider Electric

score_rationale.timing: Porsche's FE title slot is open after TAG Heuer's exit - a rare title-rights opening with a real clock.
score_rationale.capacity: ~EUR38B revenue energy-management major; title-rights capacity is comfortable.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Energy management in an all-electric championship is the cleanest possible tech-in-the-paddock fit; sustainability narrative is native.
score_rationale.urgency: An open Porsche title slot will be filled; first credible bidder shapes the deal.

prospects.headline: TAG Heuer vacated the Porsche Formula E title slot after six seasons - and an energy-management giant has never put its name on an all-electric grid.
prospects.the_case: Porsche's Formula E title position is open after TAG Heuer ended a six-season run. Schneider Electric - a ~EUR38B energy-management and industrial-tech major - has the capacity for title rights and the cleanest narrative fit in all of motorsport: energy management as the title partner of an all-electric world championship. It has never taken a motorsport title, so this is a category-defining first.
prospects.why_now: Title slots open rarely; the Porsche vacancy is a forcing function. The first credible energy/tech bidder shapes the term sheet and locks a multi-year sustainability flagship.
prospects.why_team: Porsche FE pairs premium performance with the open title slot; Schneider's energy-efficiency story maps directly onto Gen4 electric racing.
prospects.deal_architecture: Title-rights or presenting-partner tier on Porsche Formula E, minimum three years, with energy-management technical activation (paddock microgrid, efficiency storytelling) baked in.

decision_maker.title: Brand / Sponsorship leadership
decision_maker.bio: Confirm current global brand/sponsorship owner; align with the sustainability and corporate-affairs leadership who own the net-zero narrative.

prospects.opening_angle: "The only all-electric world championship just lost its title sponsor. Energy management belongs on the front of that car - and no competitor can claim that story before you do."

risks.title: B2B vs CONSUMER FIT
risks.detail: Schneider is largely B2B; title rights are high-visibility.
risks.counter: Frame as enterprise-credibility, recruiting and sustainability leadership, not consumer reach.

risks.title: PORSCHE PRICE EXPECTATION
risks.detail: A premium team title slot commands a premium.
risks.counter: Use multi-year term and technical-partner value-in-kind to balance cash outlay.
